prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which made incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single B010 prize for Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The case rests on the discovery chain and not on the six first-place rankings. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and action in humans and the incretin effect, Mojsov identified and made available the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, and Drucker defined the receptor biology and the therapeutic rationale. Large independent randomized trials in type 2 diabetes, obesity and now cardiovascular and renal outcomes show the mechanism is real and the benefit durable, so maturity is not in question. The round-1 exchange tested the configuration on the points that mattered, namely Knudsen, Mojsov's priority and the choice of a second part, and none of those arguments dislodged it. The citation names physiology and the active form as the discovery and treats the therapies as their consequence. That wording makes the allocation principled and keeps the exclusion of the drug-engineering step from reading as an oversight.
statement.case_against: The cost I carry is attribution, and round 1 did not remove it. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's engineering of long-acting agonists is a real scientific contribution, and I agree with Sandberg and Linnarsson that calling it only industrial understates it. Mojsov's priority against Habener and other early peptide workers is argued from recalled history, and the supplied record does not let this committee verify the chronology. As the chair asks, I therefore treat the Mojsov claim as probable but not demonstrated. A prize resting on a contested name has a weakness that a two-person prize such as B004 does not have. Long-term durability and safety of chronic obesity treatment are still accruing, though I do not expect that to change a prize-level judgement.

responses.point: The chair moved from the opening trio with Knudsen to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, but asks whether the citation must name the therapeutic invention and, if not, how to word it so Knudsen's exclusion does not look like an oversight.
responses.response: I agree with the move and would answer the chair's first question as follows. The citation should name the physiology and the active form of GLP-1 as the discovery and name type 2 diabetes and obesity therapy as the consequence they made possible. It should not name the long-acting agonists as an achievement of the laureates. That wording separates discovery from drug development openly, which is what several of us asked for in round 1. I would not reopen the third name for a citation that mentions therapy, because the real question is who made the discovery. I would reopen it only if a majority concluded that the prize is meant to honour the invention of the medicine itself. I would then want that said plainly and not carried by the choice of names.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps B028 as an alternative because Eshhar's chimeric receptor work lies outside the credited names and Rosenberg's adoptive transfer is broader than CAR design. He also asks how I weigh the 2018 checkpoint prize for cell therapy.
responses.response: On the 2018 prize I think CAR-T is a distinct achievement. Checkpoint blockade releases an existing T-cell response, while CAR-T gives T cells a new engineered specificity and costimulatory signalling, and the immune biology and toxicity profile differ. I do not treat 2018 as a bar. Your credit objection is the stronger point and I concede it. The credited trio combines receptor design, clinical translation and broad adoptive transfer, and a prize that leaves out an originator of the chimeric-receptor concept is more exposed than B010. I therefore withdraw any suggestion that the B028 trio is a comfortable fit. I keep B028 as my first alternative, to be used only if the committee can define the achievement narrowly enough to defend who is named. It is not strong enough to displace B010 this year.

responses.point: Sandberg would test Mojsov's role against the documented sequence of events before keeping her, and says she would move toward the chair's earlier trio if that review showed the claim to be weaker than assumed.
responses.response: I accept the test and note how little the supplied record lets us do. What is documented is that the biologically active form of GLP-1 was identified as the truncated 7-36 peptide and that this identification enabled both physiology and drug concepts. What is not documented here is the chronology among Mojsov, Habener and colleagues. I will not claim more than that. I disagree that an unresolved priority dispute should push the third place to Knudsen by default. Knudsen's claim is different in kind, since it concerns development of the drugs, and it is not a better answer to the question of who identified the peptide. If the record showed Mojsov's claim to be weaker, I would prefer a narrower two-name citation or a different discovery-side name over a development name. I do not think the evidence here warrants that, and I am keeping Mojsov.

responses.point: Linnarsson argues that the citation should be written around hormone physiology and the active peptide forms and not around drug design, so that Knudsen's exclusion reads as principled. He also treats B004 as a fallback and B028 as the first alternative.
responses.response: I agree on the citation and have kept my wording close to yours. I also agree that B028 outranks B004 as the first alternative if B010 is blocked, because B028 has approved products and years of follow-up. Your case against B004 rests only on missing clinical translation, which I think is partly fair, and I would not call that a defect of the science. I have therefore changed my second alternative from B012 to B004. In round 1 I put B012 third. The omission of Zhou and the parallel VLP priority claims that El-Manira raised make it harder to defend a three-name allocation than I had allowed. B004 now looks like the better fallback to me. It should be tested if the GLP-1 attribution fails, but not above B028 on medical grounds.

responses.point: El-Manira regards the unresolved Habener question as a cost and says that if the committee decides translation must be recognised, this should be stated openly as a choice. He proposes no two-part prize because B010 plus B028 would exceed three people.
responses.response: I agree that the Habener question cannot be settled from the evidence we have, and that any recognition of translation must be a stated choice and not implicit in the name list. I also considered a two-part configuration this round, since the chair asks whether we should. A B010 plus B028 pairing needs at least four names, so one of the GLP-1 laureates would have to be cut. I cannot name which of Holst, Drucker or Mojsov should go without damaging the citation, and B028 is itself not ready on attribution. A two-part prize would trade a strong single achievement for two contested ones. I therefore stay with one achievement and three names.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active peptide holds against Habener and other early workers. This is argued from recalled history and the supplied record does not verify the chronology, so I rely on the documented identification of GLP-1(7-36) as the active form and not on a priority ranking.
Whether the committee will accept a discovery-anchored citation that mentions therapy as a consequence and leaves out Knudsen, or will insist on naming the invention of the long-acting agonists.
For B028, whether the achievement can be defined (receptor design, clinical translation or broader adoptive transfer) so that Eshhar's omission is defensible.
I have not independently checked recent trial or priority details beyond what is in the round-1 files and my recall of the literature.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no documented personal or institutional connection to Drucker, Holst or Mojsov, or to any other credited name on the shortlist. My expertise in autoimmunity is relevant to B028 (CAR-T in autoimmune disease), but I have no personal tie to its candidates and I weigh it on the same criteria as the others. I have not inferred ties from shared institutions.
